post.description:
Creates the very first admin account from the web UI, so a fresh instance no longer
requires `docker compose exec app python -m scripts.create_admin`. Deliberately not a
general-purpose register endpoint — create_initial_admin rejects this once any user
already exists (see app/services/auth_service.py), and that rejection surfaces as a 409
via the app-wide ConflictError handler in app/main.py.

BulkImportLibraryDefaults.title: BulkImportLibraryDefaults
BulkImportLibraryDefaults.description:
Step 3 of the bulk-add dialog, applied identically to every successfully-imported
game — a deliberate subset of LibraryItemCreateRequest (just Ownership/Platform/Format/
Digital Storefront, no Price/Region/Rating Board/Notes/etc.), per the user's own scoping.

CatalogRefResponse.title: CatalogRefResponse
CatalogRefResponse.description:
Shared id+name+slug shape for genre/franchise/collection references attached to a
game — enough to display and (for franchise/collection) link to a browse page.

EmulationConfigResponse.title: EmulationConfigResponse
EmulationConfigResponse.description:
Everything the frontend needs to know about in-browser emulation up front: bundled
cores (for About's credits), which file extensions each copy format accepts (for the
upload picker's `accept` list), and the upload size cap — so none of it is duplicated
as a frontend-side list that could drift from the backend's real validation.

EventVideoResponse.title: EventVideoResponse
EventVideoResponse.description:
Shaped identically to GameVideoResponse so the frontend's existing VideoGallery
component works unmodified for events.

GameCategory.title: GameCategory
GameCategory.description:
Mirrors IGDB's numeric `games.category` field (id 0-14). Declaration order is load
bearing — `from_igdb_category_id` indexes into `list(GameCategory)` by position, so
members must stay in IGDB's exact numeric order; never reorder or insert in the middle.

GameSortOption.title: GameSortOption
GameSortOption.description:
The Games list previously had no sort options at all (always a hardcoded
Game.name ascending) — a genuinely new capability, not an extension of an existing one.

HardwareReferenceSummary.title: HardwareReferenceSummary
HardwareReferenceSummary.description:
Nested "rich data" block on Device/Accessory detail responses — only the fields not
already represented on the catalog row itself (brand/generation/official_name overlap
with Device/Accessory's own manufacturer/hardwarePlatform/officialName).

IgdbGamePreviewResponse.title: IgdbGamePreviewResponse
IgdbGamePreviewResponse.description:
A game straight from IGDB, never persisted — backs the Add Game preview page. Uses the
same field names/shapes as GameDetailResponse for everything GameAboutSection reads, so
that section renders it unchanged; nested ids are IGDB's (display keys only — nothing
here exists locally). Fields with no meaning for a not-yet-added game (parent links to
local games, rating, edition) are always empty.

IgdbReleaseRegion.title: IgdbReleaseRegion
IgdbReleaseRegion.description:
IGDB's release_dates.release_region enum (1-indexed) — the geographic market a
release date applies to (Europe/North America/Japan/Worldwide/...). Deliberately NOT
the same thing as this app's `Region` model (PAL/NTSC-U/NTSC-J media-region tracking
for the user's own physical/digital copies, see Region's docstring) — conflating the
two would silently misrepresent both. A plain enum, not a table: IGDB's own enum is
small and fixed, never user-edited, exactly like GameCategory.

SetupRequest.title: SetupRequest
SetupRequest.description:
Minimal provisioning validation that plain LoginRequest deliberately skips —
login must accept whatever's already stored, but the first-run form is the one place
that gets to reject a weak account before it's created.
